references.text: Parallel text about God visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children to the third and fourth generation, but showing mercy to thousands who love him.
Moses quotes this text almost verbatim when he prays for the people of Israel after the report of the spies.
Repetition of the message about God visiting the iniquity of the fathers, but showing mercy to thousands who love him.
Describes God's faithful love (חֶסֶד) to a thousand generations, and his retribution against those who hate him.
The psalm describes the Lord as good and willing to forgive (נֹשֵׂא עָוֺן), rich in mercy (חֶסֶד) toward all who call on him.
Refers to God's compassion and grace, and that he does not deal with us according to our sins.
Theme of forgiveness and that God does not keep a record of sin, related to נֹשֵׂא עָוֺן וָפֶשַׁע וְחַטָּאָה.
Jeremiah modifies the teaching about punishing children for their fathers' sins - in the new covenant each shall die for their own sin.
Direct reference to God's mercy to thousands and visiting the iniquity of the fathers on their children.
Ezekiel takes up and nuances the idea that children are punished for their fathers' sins - every soul that sins shall die.
Micah praises God as one who bears sin (נֹשֵׂא עָוֺן) and forgives transgression, with faithful love (חֶסֶד).
Nahum quotes that the Lord will by no means leave the guilty unpunished (וְנַקֵּה לֹא יְנַקֶּה).
Jonah cites God's attributes from Exodus 34:6-7 as the reason he fled - he knew that God is gracious.
Paul discusses God's goodness and forbearance in relation to human judgment and repentance.
Paul quotes from Exodus about God's mercy and compassion, related to his sovereign grace.
In Christ we have redemption and forgiveness of sins according to the riches of his grace.
God is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Historical illustration of the same divine character defined in Exodus.
Theological nuance distinguishing between collective consequences and individual responsibility.
Concrete example supporting the principle of individual responsibility against the background of Exodus.
Prophetic confirmation of God's overarching will for grace corresponding to the definition in Exodus.
Direct quote applying the principle of generational guilt in the context of idols.
